reason: E4 and E5 directly support that fine grains increase surface strength and improve wear resistance via more stable oxide layers, while coarse grains soften and crack. E3 supports that fine structures provide barriers to deformation and that oxide layers can be unstable, but does not directly link grain refinement to enhanced oxide stability. E1 notes oxidation effects but does not support the specific mechanism; E2 contradicts the hypothesis by showing low friction in inert environments without oxidation.
premises: Fine-grained HEA coatings have higher surface strength than coarse-grained ones
Higher surface strength promotes formation of a continuous, stable oxide/glaze layer during sliding
A continuous, stable oxide layer prevents direct metal contact and reduces adhesive/abrasive wear
Coarse-grained coatings suffer oxide layer cracking and delamination due to softening under friction heat
Grain refinement enhances uniform deformation, facilitating coherent oxide formation
